install.title: How to install
install.intro_pwa: This app is an installable site: it opens in the browser and you can add it to your home screen like a regular app, no store needed.
install.intro_apk: This app is distributed by the creator as an APK file, outside Google Play.
install.android_1: Open the app in Chrome and tap the ⋮ menu in the top-right corner.
install.android_2: Choose "Install app" or "Add to Home screen".
install.ios_1: Open the app in Safari and tap the Share button (square with arrow).
install.pc_1: Open the app in Chrome or Edge.
install.pc_2: Click the install icon on the right side of the address bar.
install.apk_2: If Android asks, allow installing apps from unknown sources.
install.apk_3: Open the downloaded file and tap Install.
install.desktop_1: Download the installer and open it.
install.not_android: This app is an APK, an Android-only format. It is not available for {device}.
install.not_available: This app is not available for {device}.
install.ios_not_safari: On iPhone and iPad only Safari can install web apps. Open this page in Safari and repeat the steps.
install.android_unknown_browser: Can't see the install option? Not every Android browser can install web apps. Try Chrome.
install.android_unknown_browser_apk: Can't see the install option? Not every Android browser can install web apps. In that case, download the APK below.
install.pc_unsupported: Your browser cannot install web apps. Use Chrome or Edge.
install.no_install_ok: Even without installing, the app works normally in the browser.

pwa.title: Install Brioverse
pwa.subtitle: {host} · opens from your home screen, no browser
pwa.installed: Brioverse is already installed on this device.
pwa.android_1: Tap the browser's ⋮ menu in the top-right corner.
pwa.android_2: Choose "Install app" or "Add to Home screen".
pwa.ios_1: In Safari, tap the Share button (square with an arrow pointing up).
pwa.ios_2: Choose "Add to Home Screen" and confirm.
pwa.pc_1: In Chrome or Edge, click the install icon on the right of the address bar.
pwa.pc_2: Confirm with "Install". Brioverse opens in its own window.

apk_warning.title: Before you download
apk_warning.p1: This APK is published by the creator and does not go through Google Play. Android will ask permission to install apps from unknown sources.
apk_warning.p2: Brioverse reviews apps before approving them, but only install if you trust the creator. The download opens the creator's official link.

dev.soon: The creator area is coming soon.
dev.title: Developer mode
dev.apply_intro: Tell us who you are and show us something you've already published. Every request is reviewed by hand to keep the store safe.
dev.name: Public creator name
dev.name_help: This is the name shown on your apps.
dev.registration_help: Optional, but it helps us confirm the company.
dev.description: About you and what you build
dev.description_help: At least {n} characters. Technologies you use, projects, experience.
dev.ph_description: E.g. I've been building installable sites (PWA) in React for 3 years. I made Poupa+ and Rota Fácil, both with over a thousand users…
dev.website_help: Where we can see your work.
dev.sample: Link to an app or project you've already published
dev.sample_help: An installable site (PWA), website or APK of yours we can open and try.
dev.repo_help: Optional. A profile with public code counts a lot in your favour.
dev.contact_help: For notices about your apps and your account.
dev.accept_pre: I have read and accept the
dev.sent: We'll review your details. The answer will show up in your account, in the Developer card.
dev.err_url: Must be a valid link starting with https://
dev.err_accept: You must accept the terms to continue.
dev.err_generic: Could not save. Please try again.
dev.not_configured: Firebase not configured: the application is only stored in this browser.
dev.pending_notice: Your application is under review. You can still correct the details.
dev.rejected_notice: Your application was rejected. Fix what's needed and resend.
dev.no_apps: You don't have any apps on Brioverse yet.
dev.submit_soon: Submitting apps from this panel is coming soon. Meanwhile, send us your app through support.
dev.no_apps_hint: Tap Publish to send your first app for review.
dev.status_pending_hint: Under review by the team. We'll notify you when it's approved.
dev.analytics_intro: Real numbers for your apps in the store: page views, Open/Download clicks and reviews.
dev.analytics_note: Numbers accumulate since publication. Daily history is coming later.
dev.no_data: No data yet. Publish an app to start seeing numbers.
dev.no_notices: No notices. When the team contacts you about an app or your account, it shows up here.
dev.exit_hint: Leave developer mode and go back to the store. You can come back from your account.
dev.admin_no_profile: You're viewing developer mode as an administrator, without a creator profile.
dev.publish_intro: Fill in your app's details. It goes to review and we'll let you know when it's in the store.
dev.publish_not_configured: Firebase not configured: the app is only stored in this browser.
dev.publish_sent: “{app}” is under review. You'll get a notice when it's approved and you can check its status in Apps.
dev.media_hint: No uploads: paste public https links to the images (GitHub, your site, a CDN). The link must open the image itself; Google Drive, Dropbox, GitHub and Imgur share pages are converted automatically.
dev.f_short_help: One sentence. Shown in lists and cards.
dev.ph_short: E.g. Group savings, simple and transparent.
dev.f_full_help: What it does, who it's for, how it works. Shown on the app page.
dev.f_keywords_help: Comma-separated, up to 10. They help search.
dev.f_appUrl_help: This is what the “Open” button opens.
dev.f_apkUrl_help: E.g. GitHub Releases. Must be https and end with .apk.
dev.f_desktopUrl_help: Windows, Mac or Linux. Shown in the “How to install” guide on computers.
dev.f_icon_help: Square, at least 512×512, PNG or SVG.
dev.f_shots_help: At least {n}, up to {max}. Preferably portrait (9:16).
dev.f_confirm: I confirm I own the rights to this app, the links are safe, and I comply with the
dev.f_version_help: E.g. 1.0.0. Change it whenever you release an update.
dev.f_changelog_help: What changed. Shown on the app page and in the notice people who have the app receive.
dev.f_changelog_help_create: Optional at launch. Shown on the app page under “What's new”.
dev.ph_changelog: E.g. Dark mode, bug fixes and better speed.
dev.version_notice: Saving with version {v} sends an update notice to everyone who has the app.
dev.err_changelog: Say what changed in this version.
dev.edit_intro: Change what you need. If you change the version or write what's new, people who have the app get a notice.
dev.edit_sent: “{app}” is now version {v}. People who have the app will see the update notice.
dev.edit_disabled: This app was disabled by the team and cannot be edited.
dev.edit_rejected: This app was rejected. Saving sends it back for review.
dev.app_not_found: This app is not yours or no longer exists.
dev.paused_hint: Paused by you. Hidden from the store until you resume it.
dev.delete_text: The app leaves the store for good, with its reviews and numbers. This cannot be undone.
dev.err_image: This link does not load as an image. Use the direct file link (it opens only the image, usually ending in .png, .jpg or .webp).
dev.err_shots: Add at least {n} screenshots with valid links.

admin.title: Admin panel
admin.disable_text: The app disappears from the store. The creator receives this reason as a notice in their account.
admin.reject_text: The applicant receives this reason and can fix the details and resend.
admin.revoke_text: The creator loses developer mode and receives this reason. Their apps stay as they are: disable them in the Apps tab if needed.
admin.reason_ph: Explain the reason. The creator will read this.
admin.demo: Demo mode: without Firebase configured, changes are not saved.
admin.error: Could not save. Check the connection and the Firestore rules.
